Langfuse is an open source AI engineering platform for agent evals and observability. It is one open platform for every AI call your company makes and every agent your teams build: track usage and costs, trace and evaluate agents, and use production data to ship better AI. Use Langfuse Cloud or self-host in minutes; Langfuse is battle-tested at scale.

🧑‍💻 We're hiring

Interested in contributing to Langfuse full-time? Langfuse is growing fast (we doubled the team in the last 6 months). Since January 2026 we're part of ClickHouse. We hire remotely, with offices in Berlin, San Francisco, Amsterdam, and New York. See open roles →

✨ Core Features

  • AI Observability: Instrument your app and start ingesting traces to Langfuse, thereby tracking LLM calls and other relevant logic in your app such as retrieval, embedding, or agent actions. Inspect and debug complex logs and user sessions. Built on OpenTelemetry. Try the interactive demo to see this in action.

  • Prompt Management helps you centrally manage, version control, and collaboratively iterate on your prompts. Thanks to strong caching on server and client side, you can iterate on prompts without adding latency to your application. The LLM Playground lets you test prompts and model configurations; when you see a bad result in tracing, you can jump straight to the playground to iterate on it.

  • Skill Management (beta) brings versioning and labels to agent skills: a SKILL.md with task instructions plus optional supporting files. Promote or roll back versions without changing application code, and link skill versions to the traces they produced.

  • Evaluations are key to the AI agent development workflow, and Langfuse adapts to your needs. It supports LLM-as-a-judge, code evaluators, user feedback collection, manual labeling, and custom evaluation pipelines via APIs/SDKs. Use Datasets and Experiments to build test sets and benchmarks for pre-deployment testing and continuous improvement.

  • AI Gateway (beta) gives your organization one endpoint for calls to your model providers. Keep provider credentials in one place, hand out per-user or service account gateway keys, approve models centrally, track AI spend per user, key, and model, and record every call as a Langfuse trace.

  • Metrics and Dashboards: Track latency, cost, and quality across any dimension with custom dashboards, the metrics API, and alerts.

  • Comprehensive API: Langfuse is frequently used to power bespoke AI engineering workflows while using the building blocks provided by Langfuse via the API. An OpenAPI spec, typed SDKs for Python and JS/TS, the Langfuse CLI, and the Langfuse Agent Skill for coding agents are available.

📦 Deploy Langfuse

Langfuse Cloud

Managed deployment by the Langfuse team, generous free tier, no credit card required.

Sign up for Langfuse Cloud →

Self-Host Langfuse

Run Langfuse on your own infrastructure:

  • Docker Compose: Run Langfuse on your own machine or a single virtual machine in 5 minutes. The guide also covers configuring Docker log rotation so container logs don't fill up the disk.

    # Get a copy of the latest Langfuse repository
git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse.git
cd langfuse

# Run the langfuse docker compose
docker compose up

  • Kubernetes (Helm): Run Langfuse on a Kubernetes cluster using Helm. This is the preferred production deployment.

  • Terraform Templates: AWS, Azure, GCP

  • Community-maintained: Render, Railway

See self-hosting documentation to learn more about architecture and configuration options.

[!TIP] Self-hosting Langfuse? Subscribe to the self-hosting update list to get an email about important features and new releases for open source Langfuse — self-hosting updates only, no marketing.

🚀 Quickstart

Instrument your app and start ingesting traces to Langfuse, thereby tracking LLM calls and other relevant logic in your app such as retrieval, embedding, or agent actions. Inspect and debug complex logs and user sessions.

🤖 Agentic installation (recommended)

Install the Langfuse Agent Skill to let your coding agent access all Langfuse features, then ask it to add tracing to your application:

Install the Langfuse Agent Skill from github.com/langfuse/skills
and use it to add tracing to this application with Langfuse
following best practices.

You can also install the skill with the skills CLI (npx skills add langfuse/skills --skill "langfuse") or the Langfuse Cursor plugin. If your agent supports MCP, add the Langfuse Docs MCP server (https://langfuse.com/api/mcp, no authentication) so it can look up current documentation while it works. See the get started guide for details.

🛠️ Manual installation

1️⃣ Create new project

  1. Create Langfuse account or self-host
  2. Create a new project
  3. Create new API credentials in the project settings

2️⃣ Log your first LLM call

The @observe() decorator makes it easy to trace any Python LLM application. In this quickstart we also use the Langfuse OpenAI integration to automatically capture all model parameters.

[!TIP] Not using OpenAI? Visit our documentation to learn how to log other models and frameworks.

pip install langfuse openai

LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY="sk-lf-..."
LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY="pk-lf-..."
LANGFUSE_BASE_URL="https://cloud.langfuse.com" # 🇪🇺 EU region
# LANGFUSE_BASE_URL="https://us.cloud.langfuse.com" # 🇺🇸 US region
# LANGFUSE_BASE_URL="https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com" # 🇯🇵 Japan region
# LANGFUSE_BASE_URL="https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com" # ⚕️ HIPAA region

from langfuse import observe
from langfuse.openai import openai # OpenAI integration

@observe()
def story():
    return openai.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is Langfuse?"}],
    ).choices[0].message.content

@observe()
def main():
    return story()

main()

💭 Support

Finding an answer to your question:

  • Our documentation is the best place to start looking for answers. It is comprehensive, and we invest significant time into maintaining it. You can also suggest edits to the docs via GitHub.
  • Langfuse FAQs where the most common questions are answered.
  • Use "Ask AI" to get instant answers to your questions.

Support Channels:

  • Ask any question in our public Q&A on GitHub Discussions. Please include as much detail as possible (e.g. code snippets, screenshots, background information) to help us understand your question.
  • Request a feature on GitHub Discussions.
  • Report a Bug on GitHub Issues.
  • For time-sensitive queries, ping us via the in-app chat widget.

🤝 Contributing

Your contributions are welcome!

  • Vote on Ideas in GitHub Discussions.
  • Raise and comment on Issues.
  • Open a PR - see CONTRIBUTING.md for details on how to setup a development environment.
